subject: run level summarisation is default in quant?

messages.author: 5ed7d1cb176d5a15
messages.subject: run level summarisation is default in quant?
parts:
Hey

I wanted to verify if the current practice in MSstats  is to always do run-level summaristation before testing for differential expression.

1) So, peptide intensities are summarised with TMP to 1 protein intensity value for each run in the experiment.
2) These protein level intensities values are used in a linear model to estimate the effect of eg.  treatments on that protein (differential expression between treatments)

If so, are you still in favor of model peptide-level intensities (without summarisation) or do you suggest against that?

I believed, in the past, MSstats was using linear models directly on  peptide intensities. Right?

Thanks in advance

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: run level summarisation is default in quant?
parts:
1) Yes
2) Yes

MSstats v2 used peptide or transition-level intensities. But, MSstats v3 does not support the model with peptide or transition-level intensities.

HTH

- Meena

messages.subject: Re: run level summarisation is default in quant?

We are working for manuscript from MSstats v3. Hope that it can be published soon. At this moment, you can use original msstats publication.

There are several links for training course. Especially, May Institute course talk about MSstats in most detailed. (https://computationalproteomics.ccis.northeastern.edu > material pages). Hope that it can answer your question.

- Meena
